column9: Small, everyday tasks, usually involving maintenance or repair around the house.
column10: I went over to help my parents with a few little odd jobs.
column11: He earns some extra money by doing odd jobs for his neighbours.
column12: The handyman was hired to do various odd jobs around the office.

column9: To use a good situation to get the best possible result or experience.
column10: I wanted to really kind of make the most of that quality time together.
column11: We only have three days in Paris, so let's make the most of it.
column12: She makes the most of her free time by reading and studying.

column9: Difficult to do or use because it involves small, delicate parts or movements.
column10: Those spotlights in the ceiling are very annoying and fiddly to change.
column11: Repairing a watch is a very fiddly job.
column12: I hate tying these shoelaces; the knot is too fiddly.

column9: A hand tool used for gripping and turning nuts or bolts.
column10: I grabbed a few spanners, and the first one I used was exactly the right size.
column11: Can you pass me the spanner so I can tighten this pipe?
column12: He threw a spanner in the works by changing the entire project plan.

column9: A search that is completely unsuccessful and a waste of time because the thing being searched for does not exist or is somewhere else.
column10: It was a wild goose chase trying to find a replacement tyre in that remote area.
column11: The police realized the anonymous tip was just a wild goose chase.
column12: I spent all day on a wild goose chase looking for a specific brand of tea.

column9: Thinking carefully and quietly about past events or deep ideas.
column10: As you get older, you become more reflective about your life and family history.
column11: She was in a quiet, reflective mood after reading the letter.
column12: The documentary takes a reflective look at the consequences of the war.

column9: (Of a thought or idea) to come into someone's mind.
column10: When you're young, it just doesn't occur to you to ask your parents about their youth.
column11: It suddenly occurred to me that I had left the oven on.
column12: Did it ever occur to him that she might be upset?

column9: To walk through water or other liquid with some effort.
column10: He had to get into the water up to his chest and wade ashore.
column11: We waded across the shallow river to reach the other side.
column12: They spent the afternoon wading in the rock pools at the beach.

column9: A place frequently visited by a specified person.
column10: We took him on a tour around all his childhood haunts.
column11: This pub used to be one of my favorite haunts when I was at university.
column12: The detective visited the criminal's usual haunts to find clues.

column9: To start to organize yourself so that you do things in an effective way.
column10: My father finally got his act together after the war and decided what he was going to do.
column11: You need to get your act together if you want to pass this exam.
column12: She needs to get her act together and find a proper job.

column9: A person's livelihood or main source of income; the most basic, fundamental aspect of a job.
column10: Writing letters and taking dictation was the absolute bread and butter of the job.
column11: Fixing laptops is the bread and butter of our IT business.
column12: I enjoy painting, but teaching is my bread and butter.

column9: A system of rapid handwriting using symbols or abbreviations to represent letters, words, or phrases.
column10: The boss would dictate the letter, and you would use shorthand to write it down.
column11: She took notes in shorthand so she wouldn't miss anything the speaker said.
column12: The term 'burnout' has become a shorthand for extreme workplace exhaustion.

column9: A large quantity of something, typically paper or writing.
column10: Sometimes there were reams and reams of letters to type.
column11: She had to read through reams of documents before the trial.
column12: He wrote reams of poetry that was never published.

column9: To show anger, worry, or excitement that is unnecessary or greater than the situation deserves.
column10: I was very meek and mild and I wouldn't dream of making a fuss.
column11: Please don't make a fuss over me; I'm perfectly fine.
column12: The customer made a huge fuss about the slight delay in service.

column9: Someone who cares a lot about whether other people like them, and always wants others to approve of their actions.
column10: I was brought up to be a people pleaser, always behaving myself and staying quiet.
column11: As a people pleaser, she finds it impossible to say no to extra work.
column12: He realized that being a people pleaser was making him miserable.

column9: An old-fashioned rule that children should be quiet and well-behaved around adults.
column10: The Victorian idea was that children should be seen and not heard.
column11: When I was growing up, kids were meant to be seen and not heard.
column12: She sat quietly in the corner, obeying the 'seen and not heard' rule of her strict grandparents.

column9: Practical intelligence or common sense.
column10: He had the nous to go off and do adventurous things that I didn't want to do.
column11: She showed a lot of political nous during the campaign.
column12: You need a bit of business nous to succeed in this industry.

column9: An artificial bank raised above the immediately surrounding land to route a railway or road.
column10: The house had a steep railway embankment at the end of the garden.
column11: They walked along the river embankment on a sunny afternoon.
column12: The train tracks ran along a high grass embankment.

column9: A period of uncertainty and confusion in which a person's sense of identity becomes insecure.
column10: Not knowing what career to choose felt like a real identity crisis.
column11: Many teenagers go through an identity crisis as they grow up.
column12: After retiring from sports, the athlete suffered a severe identity crisis.

column9: A situation where there are as many advantages as there are problems, making the end result the same.
column10: Both having a career and staying at home have pros and cons; it's swings and roundabouts.
column11: If we take the toll road we pay more, but save petrol, so it's swings and roundabouts.
column12: You lose some money on shipping, but save on packaging, so it's all swings and roundabouts.

column9: The invisible, non-tangible cognitive effort involved in managing a household, family, or demanding tasks.
column10: The mental load is much greater when you have to balance a demanding career and children.
column11: Sharing household chores doesn't always split the mental load of planning everything.
column12: She felt exhausted by the mental load of organizing the family's schedule.

column9: Making you feel very tired; exhausting (British English).
column10: I can't do the gardening anymore because it's absolutely knackering.
column11: It was a knackering journey, and we just wanted to sleep.
column12: Playing football for 90 minutes is quite a knackering experience.

column9: To stay the same and not grow or develop.
column10: Keep interested in everything and don't stagnate as you get older.
column11: Without investment, the local economy will continue to stagnate.
column12: He changed jobs because he felt his career was beginning to stagnate.

column9: To stop criticizing or being too hard on someone (or oneself).
column10: I'll give my future self a break and say, don't worry about it.
column11: Give him a break; he's only been doing this job for a week.
column12: I wish the press would give the young actress a break.

column9: Left in a place from which you cannot escape.
column10: The radio show features guests who imagine being marooned on a desert island.
column11: The car broke down, leaving us marooned in the middle of nowhere.
column12: During the flood, several families were marooned on the roofs of their houses.

column9: A speech, piece of writing, or poem containing great praise, especially for someone who recently died.
column10: I recorded an episode called 'Eulogy for Dennis' after my grandfather passed away.
column11: He delivered a moving eulogy at his best friend's funeral.
column12: The newspaper published a beautiful eulogy celebrating the late author's life.

column9: To talk for a long time about things that are not important.
column10: It's a conversation where we generally witter on about a number of different things.
column11: I wish he would stop wittering on about his boring stamp collection.
column12: She spent the whole evening wittering on about the weather.

column9: To share the same feelings as someone else, or to behave in the same way as someone else.
column10: It's always nice when listeners reciprocate by sharing things about themselves.
column11: Sadly, my feelings for her were not reciprocated.
column12: They invited us to dinner, so we should reciprocate and invite them next week.

column9: To give your full attention to the situation you are in, and not worry about the past or the future.
column10: When I was young, I just lived in the moment and didn't plan my career too much.
column11: She tries to live in the moment rather than stressing about what might happen tomorrow.
column12: It's important to live in the moment and enjoy the present experiences.

column9: To use the good things in a situation; to make good use of an opportunity.
column10: I probably didn't take advantage of the university facilities as much as I could have.
column11: Make sure you take advantage of the free training courses offered at work.
column12: We took advantage of the sunny weather and went for a long hike.
